quests.question: Every afternoon, the delivery van drives ___ the warehouse on the edge of town.
quests.targetSentence: Every afternoon, the delivery van drives to the warehouse on the edge of town.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'To' shows movement toward a destination that is reached; the trip is completed daily, unlike 'toward', which would leave the arrival open.
quests.nativeTip: This preposition points toward a destination the van actually reaches each day.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'to' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Every afternoon, the delivery van drives to the warehouse on the edge of town.'

quests.question: The flight departs ___ Gate 14 at six o'clock.
quests.targetSentence: The flight departs from Gate 14 at six o'clock.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'From' marks the starting point of a journey, such as a flight departing from a particular gate.
quests.nativeTip: Think about where something begins, not where it ends up.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The flight departs from Gate 14 at six o'clock.'

quests.question: The passengers filed ___ the departure lounge as their gate was announced.
quests.targetSentence: The passengers filed into the departure lounge as their gate was announced.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Into' shows movement toward the inside of a place; 'in' would only describe their position once they had already arrived.
quests.nativeTip: The travelers are moving toward the inside of the room, not simply standing there.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'into' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The passengers filed into the departure lounge as their gate was announced.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs into
quests.question: She hurried ___ the elevator just before the doors closed.
quests.targetSentence: She hurried into the elevator just before the doors closed.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Into' describes movement toward the inside of the elevator. Since she was still moving as the doors nearly shut, this is motion, not a finished position.
quests.nativeTip: The doors were about to close, so she was still moving at that moment.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'into' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She hurried into the elevator just before the doors closed.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs into
quests.spatialHierarchy: Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)
quests.question: By the time we called, she was already ___ the elevator, on her way up.
quests.targetSentence: By the time we called, she was already in the elevator, on her way up.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'In' describes a completed location rather than the act of arriving there — she was already inside the elevator, not entering it.
quests.nativeTip: By the time the call happened, the movement was already finished.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'in' (Enclosed Space / Volume (e.g. in the room)) ➔ 'By the time we called, she was already in the elevator, on her way up.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: in vs into
quests.question: The children rushed ___ the swimming pool the moment the lifeguard arrived.
quests.targetSentence: The children rushed into the swimming pool the moment the lifeguard arrived.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Into' fits because 'rushed' describes the movement of entering the pool, the same pattern shown with the elevator earlier.
quests.nativeTip: Notice the verb 'rushed', which suggests motion rather than simply existing somewhere.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'into' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The children rushed into the swimming pool the moment the lifeguard arrived.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on vs onto
quests.question: The cat jumped ___ the kitchen counter to steal some fish.
quests.targetSentence: The cat jumped onto the kitchen counter to steal some fish.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Onto' describes movement toward a surface. 'On' would only describe the cat's position once it had already landed there.
quests.nativeTip: The cat starts on the floor and ends up on the counter — that change of surface matters.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'onto' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The cat jumped onto the kitchen counter to steal some fish.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on vs onto
quests.question: The keys have been sitting ___ the counter all morning.
quests.targetSentence: The keys have been sitting on the counter all morning.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'On' is used for a static position on a surface. Since the keys 'have been sitting' there, there is no movement to justify 'onto'.
quests.nativeTip: Nothing is moving in this sentence — the keys have simply been resting there since morning.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'on' (Surface Contact (e.g. on the table)) ➔ 'The keys have been sitting on the counter all morning.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: on vs onto
quests.question: Using the ladder, he climbed ___ the roof to fix the antenna.
quests.targetSentence: Using the ladder, he climbed onto the roof to fix the antenna.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Onto' shows movement to the top of a surface, matching the action of climbing up with a ladder.
quests.nativeTip: Using the ladder tells you this is about getting up there, not being there already.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'onto' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Using the ladder, he climbed onto the roof to fix the antenna.'

quests.question: She grabbed her umbrella and stepped ___ the taxi.
quests.targetSentence: She grabbed her umbrella and stepped out of the taxi.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Out of' describes movement from inside an enclosed space, like a taxi, to the outside.
quests.nativeTip: She is leaving an enclosed space — think about what the inside of a taxi is like.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'out of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'She grabbed her umbrella and stepped out of the taxi.'

quests.question: Please get ___ the escalator quickly once you reach the top.
quests.targetSentence: Please get off the escalator quickly once you reach the top.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Off' is used for surfaces and vehicles you stand on rather than sit inside, such as escalators, buses, or bikes.
quests.nativeTip: Public transport and moving surfaces like escalators use a different word than enclosed spaces do.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'off' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Please get off the escalator quickly once you reach the top.'

quests.question: He pulled a crumpled receipt ___ his coat pocket.
quests.targetSentence: He pulled a crumpled receipt out of his coat pocket.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Out of' fits because a pocket, like a taxi, is an enclosed space that something is removed from.
quests.nativeTip: A pocket is a small enclosed space, just like the taxi earlier.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'out of' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He pulled a crumpled receipt out of his coat pocket.'

quests.question: The train passed ___ three tunnels before reaching the coast.
quests.targetSentence: The train passed through three tunnels before reaching the coast.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' is used for movement inside a three-dimensional space that surrounds you, like a tunnel.
quests.nativeTip: Tunnels surround a train on every side, not just underneath.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The train passed through three tunnels before reaching the coast.'

quests.question: We walked ___ the bridge to reach the old town.
quests.targetSentence: We walked across the bridge to reach the old town.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Across' describes movement from one side of an open area to the other, such as a bridge over a river.
quests.nativeTip: A bridge connects one side of open space to another.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'across' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We walked across the bridge to reach the old town.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: through vs across
quests.question: A narrow footpath cuts ___ the forest, saving almost an hour.
quests.targetSentence: A narrow footpath cuts through the forest, saving almost an hour.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' fits enclosed, surrounding spaces like a forest, while 'across' better suits a flat, open area such as a field.
quests.nativeTip: A forest surrounds a path on every side, unlike an open field or square.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'A narrow footpath cuts through the forest, saving almost an hour.'

quests.question: Cyclists were riding ___ the river, enjoying the cool evening air.
quests.targetSentence: Cyclists were riding along the river, enjoying the cool evening air.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Along' describes movement that follows the length of something, like a road or a riverbank.
quests.nativeTip: The cyclists are following the line of the riverbank, not crossing it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'along' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Cyclists were riding along the river, enjoying the cool evening air.'

quests.question: The bus drove ___ our stop without slowing down.
quests.targetSentence: The bus drove past our stop without slowing down.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Past' shows movement beyond a fixed point without stopping there.
quests.nativeTip: The bus never stops here — it simply continues beyond this point.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'past' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The bus drove past our stop without slowing down.'

quests.question: We strolled ___ the beach, collecting shells as we went.
quests.targetSentence: We strolled along the beach, collecting shells as we went.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Along' fits again here, since walking along a beach means following its length.
quests.nativeTip: Like the cyclists earlier, this movement follows the edge of something.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'along' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'We strolled along the beach, collecting shells as we went.'

quests.question: The hikers pushed ___ the summit despite the strong wind.
quests.targetSentence: The hikers pushed toward the summit despite the strong wind.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Toward' shows direction without confirming arrival, which fits hikers still struggling against strong wind.
quests.nativeTip: The wind is fighting them, so reaching the top isn't guaranteed yet.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'toward' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The hikers pushed toward the summit despite the strong wind.'

quests.question: The dog suddenly bolted ___ the fireworks display.
quests.targetSentence: The dog suddenly bolted away from the fireworks display.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Away from' shows movement in the opposite direction from something, such as a frightening noise.
quests.nativeTip: Loud noises usually make animals want distance, not closeness.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'away from' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The dog suddenly bolted away from the fireworks display.'

quests.question: Slowly, the ship turned ___ the harbor entrance.
quests.targetSentence: Slowly, the ship turned toward the harbor entrance.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Toward' describes movement in the direction of something, here the harbor entrance the ship is aiming for.
quests.nativeTip: The ship is adjusting its course, aiming itself at the entrance.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'toward' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Slowly, the ship turned toward the harbor entrance.'

quests.question: The tour guide led us ___ the old fortress before lunch.
quests.targetSentence: The tour guide led us around the old fortress before lunch.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Around' describes movement that circles or surrounds something, like walking around a fortress's perimeter.
quests.nativeTip: The tour follows the outer edge of the fortress rather than going inside it.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'around' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The tour guide led us around the old fortress before lunch.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: across vs around
quests.question: Rather than crossing the square, we walked ___ it to avoid the crowd.
quests.targetSentence: Rather than crossing the square, we walked around it to avoid the crowd.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Around' is correct because the group avoided cutting across the square directly, choosing a path that circled it instead.
quests.nativeTip: The sentence already tells you they avoided going straight through.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'around' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Rather than crossing the square, we walked around it to avoid the crowd.'

quests.question: The plane flew ___ the airport twice before landing.
quests.targetSentence: The plane flew around the airport twice before landing.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Around' captures the circular motion of a plane looping the airport before landing.
quests.nativeTip: Instead of landing right away, the plane makes a loop first.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'around' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The plane flew around the airport twice before landing.'

quests.question: Commuters squeezed ___ the crowded carriage just as the doors began to close.
quests.targetSentence: Commuters squeezed into the crowded carriage just as the doors began to close.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Into' shows the commuters moving toward the inside of the carriage while the doors are still closing.
quests.nativeTip: The doors are about to shut, so this is happening mid-boarding.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'into' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Commuters squeezed into the crowded carriage just as the doors began to close.'

quests.question: He hopped ___ his bike and pedaled off.
quests.targetSentence: He hopped onto his bike and pedaled off.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Onto' describes the movement of mounting a bike, a surface you sit on top of rather than inside.
quests.nativeTip: First he gets on top of the bike, then he starts moving.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'onto' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'He hopped onto his bike and pedaled off.'

quests.question: Remember to get ___ the train at the next stop, not this one.
quests.targetSentence: Remember to get off the train at the next stop, not this one.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Off' is the standard word for leaving vehicles like trains, buses, or bikes, while 'out of' is reserved for enclosed vehicles like cars.
quests.nativeTip: Trains and other public transport use a different word than cars do for exiting.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'off' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'Remember to get off the train at the next stop, not this one.'

quests.question: The removal team carried the sofa ___ the front door and down the steps.
quests.targetSentence: The removal team carried the sofa through the front door and down the steps.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Through' fits movement through an opening like a doorway, distinct from 'into', which would suggest entering an enclosed space rather than passing through a gap.
quests.nativeTip: A doorway is an opening you pass inside of, not a surface or a container.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'through' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The removal team carried the sofa through the front door and down the steps.'

quests.question: After circling twice, the plane finally taxied ___ the runway for takeoff.
quests.targetSentence: After circling twice, the plane finally taxied onto the runway for takeoff.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Onto' shows movement toward a surface — the plane moving from the taxiway to the runway itself.
quests.nativeTip: The runway is a surface the plane needs to get on top of before takeoff.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'onto' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'After circling twice, the plane finally taxied onto the runway for takeoff.'

quests.conceptTitle: Preposition Radar: Contrast: across vs past
quests.question: The runner sprinted ___ the finish line, arms raised in victory.
quests.targetSentence: The runner sprinted across the finish line, arms raised in victory.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Across' emphasizes crossing the finish line itself, while 'past' would only suggest going beyond it without that sense of crossing.
quests.nativeTip: Crossing a specific line matters more here than simply passing a general area.
quests.visualAnchor: 🧭 Preposition 'across' (Direction & Spatial Relationship) ➔ 'The runner sprinted across the finish line, arms raised in victory.'
